title_en: Cargill International Co., Ltd. v. Fujian Jinshi Oil Processing Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over a sales contract
ruling_gist_en: In the case where the debtor's conduct harms the creditor's exercise of rights, the methods for the creditor to protect its rights are: first, to exercise the creditor's revocation right under Article 74(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting the People's Court to revoke the relevant contract concluded by the debtor; second, to request the People's Court to confirm that the relevant contract concluded by the debtor is void under Article 52(2) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over sales contract; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Fujian Province; legal person; foreign-invested enterprise; Contract Law; creditor's revocation right; contract void; malicious collusion; partial support; asset transfer; evasion of debts; good faith; contract dispute; dispute over sales contract with oil company limited et al.
full_text_en:
Cargill International SA v. Fujian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over sales contract

【Ruling Summary】

Where a debtor's conduct impairs the creditor's ability to exercise its claims, the creditor may protect its claims by either (1) exercising its right of rescission under Article 74, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting the people's court to rescind the relevant contract entered into by the debtor; or (2) requesting the people's court to confirm that the relevant contract entered into by the debtor is void under Article 52, item (2) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Min Si Zhong Zi No. 1

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Fujian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd. Address: Within Zhangzhou Development Zone, China Merchants Group Zhangzhou Development Zone, Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Wang Zhengliang, Chairperson of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xuexian, Lawyer with Liaoning Hengxin Law Office.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Zhongfang Grain and Oil (Fujian) Co., Ltd. Address: No. 129, China Merchants Avenue, China Merchants Group Zhangzhou Development Zone, Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yuxi, Chairperson of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xuexian, Lawyer with Liaoning Hengxin Law Office.

Appellant (Third Party at First Instance): Zhangzhou Development Zone Huifengyuan Trade Co., Ltd. Address: No. 23, Xiangjiang Road, China Merchants Group Zhangzhou Development Zone, Zhangzhou City, Fujian Province, People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yuxi, Chairperson of the Board of Directors.

Agent ad litem: Wang Xuexian, Lawyer with Liaoning Hengxin Law Office.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Cargill International SA. Address: 14 Rue de Normandie, Geneva, Switzerland.

Representative: Neal Sawatzke, Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zeng Jianhuang, Lawyer with Beijing Shangheng (Xi'an) Law Office.

Agent ad litem: Xie Zhenhua, Lawyer with Beijing Shangheng (Xi'an) Law Office.

The Appellants, Fujian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Fujian Jinshi Company), Zhongfang Grain and Oil (Fujian) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Zhongfang Fujian Company), and Zhangzhou Development Zone Huifengyuan Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Huifengyuan Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2007) Min Chu Zi No. 37 rendered by the Fujian High People's Court on October 23, 2011, in the case of dispute over a sales contract with the Appellee, Cargill International SA (hereinafter Cargill Company). The case was appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Chen Jizhong, Judge Gao Xiaoli, and Acting Judge Shen Hongyu, and held a public hearing on February 27, 2012. The joint Agent ad litem of the Appellants, Wang Xuexian, and the Agent ad litem of the Appellee, Xie Zhenhua, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance: Cargill Company and Fujian Jinshi Company, as well as Dalian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd., Shenyang Jinshi Soybean Industry Co., Ltd., Sichuan Jinshi Oil Meal Co., Ltd., Beijing Kema Meijia Grain and Oil Co., Ltd., and Yifeng Hong Kong Limited (these six companies hereinafter collectively referred to as the Jinshi Group), had a long-standing commercial cooperative relationship. Between April and June 2004, the Jinshi Group, due to financial difficulties, failed to pay Cargill Company for goods in a timely manner, leading to a series of commercial disputes between the parties. After repeated negotiations without resolution, in September 2004, Cargill Company submitted the aforementioned disputes to the International Federation of Oil, Seed and Fats Associations (FOSFA) for arbitration. During the arbitration process, on June 26, 2005, Cargill Company and the Jinshi Group entered into a Settlement Agreement and its ancillary documents to resolve all disputes between them in a package deal. Xu Jianfei signed on behalf of Beijing Kema Meijia Grain and Oil Co., Ltd., and Wang Zhengliang signed on behalf of the remaining five companies. The Settlement Agreement provided that the Jinshi Group would repay the debts in installments over five years and would mortgage all assets of Fujian Jinshi Company, including land use rights, buildings and fixtures, all equipment, and other property, to Cargill Company as security for the repayment of the aforementioned debts. The Settlement Agreement also provided that the parties would cooperate to expedite the issuance of a FOSFA arbitration award to confirm the repayment arrangement in the Settlement Agreement. On October 10, 2005, FOSFA issued Arbitration Award No. 3929 based on the aforementioned Settlement Agreement. Due to a slight discrepancy between the award and the agreement of the parties, FOSFA issued a corrected award in November of the same year. On March 6, 2006, Lou Yaohui, an authorized representative of Cargill Company, sent a fax to Fujian Jinshi Company and Dalian Hualiang Enterprise Group, stating: With regard to the mortgage of Fujian Jinshi Company's assets, although no affirmative response was received from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange, it agreed that we could submit an application for mortgage assets and provide relevant documents for further review. Please provide the latest asset appraisal report and balance sheet from Fujian Jinshi Company so that we can proceed with the next steps. Because the Jinshi Group failed to perform its obligations under FOSFA Arbitration Award No. 3929, and Fujian Jinshi Company did not cooperate with the asset mortgage, Cargill Company applied in May 2006 to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court of Fujian Province (hereinafter Xiamen Intermediate Court) for recognition and enforcement of FOSFA Arbitration Award No. 3929. After review, the Xiamen Intermediate Court issued Civil Ruling (2006) Xia Min Ren Zi No. 29 on June 26, 2007, recognizing and agreeing to enforce the legal effect of FOSFA Arbitration Award No. 3929, and ordering the Jinshi Group to pay Cargill Company a debt of USD 13.37 million. After this ruling took effect, Cargill Company applied to the Xiamen Intermediate Court for compulsory enforcement.

On May 8, 2006, Fujian Jinshi Company and Fujian Tianyuan Bio-protein Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Tianyuan Company) signed a Contract for Sale of State-owned Land Use Rights and Assets, stipulating that Fujian Jinshi Company would sell all of its fixed assets, including state-owned land use rights, plant buildings, office buildings, and oil production equipment, to Tianyuan Company at a total price of RMB 25.69 million (unless otherwise specified, all amounts are in RMB). Among them, the state-owned land use rights were valued at RMB 4.64 million, and the buildings and equipment were valued at RMB 21.05 million. The full payment was to be made within 30 days after the contract became effective. Wang Xiaoqi and Liu Feng signed the contract on behalf of Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, respectively, as their legal representatives. On April 30, 2006, Fujian Jinshi Company commissioned Dalian Daxin Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. to appraise the value of the oil production equipment it intended to transfer. The firm issued an Asset Appraisal Report on May 5, 2006, concluding that the appraised value of the machinery and equipment assets provided by Fujian Jinshi Company as of the appraisal base date of April 30, 2006, was RMB 15,685,400. On May 8, 2006, Fujian Jinshi Company commissioned Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. to appraise its state-owned land use rights, plant buildings, office buildings, and other structures. Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued an Appraisal Report on November 20, 2006, concluding that as of the appraisal base date of May 8, 2006, the appraised value of the entrusted assets was RMB 10,004,607. On June 15, 2006, Tianyuan Company transferred RMB 25 million from account No. 37417 at the Zhangzhou Branch of the Agricultural Bank of China to account No. 35734 of Fujian Jinshi Company at the same bank. On the same day, Fujian Jinshi Company transferred two amounts of RMB 13 million and RMB 12 million from that account to the account of Dalian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd., under the description of current account payments. On December 31, 2001, Fujian Jinshi Company signed a Contract for Transfer of Land Use Rights with China Merchants Group Zhangzhou Development Zone Co., Ltd., stipulating a land transfer price of RMB 100,000 per mu, totaling RMB 4.821 million. After paying the full amount, Fujian Jinshi Company obtained the state-owned land use rights over the 32,138 square meters of land involved. On May 10, 2006, Tianyuan Company and Fujian Jinshi Company stamped the List of Subject Matter of Sale (Handover) to complete the handover of the aforementioned subject matter of sale. Tianyuan Company obtained the state-owned land use rights certificate for the said 32,138 square meters of land on June 19, 2006.

Dalian Hualiang Enterprise Group was established on December 16, 2001, with its parent company being Dalian Hualiang Enterprise Group Co., Ltd. Its members included five subsidiaries, such as Fujian Jinshi Company, Dalian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd., and Dalian Yiliang Trade Co., Ltd., as well as six other member companies.

Fujian Jinshi Company was established on October 18, 2001, with an initial registered capital of RMB 10 million. Its shareholders were: Dalian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd. (legal representative Wang Zhengliang) holding 60%, Wang Xiaoli holding 20%, and Wang Xiaoqi holding 20%. The legal representative was Wang Xiaoli, Chairperson of the Board. On August 10, 2002, the registered capital was changed to RMB 120 million. The shareholders changed to: Dalian Hualiang Enterprise Group Co., Ltd. (legal representative Wang Zhengfeng) holding 37.5%, Wang Xiaoli holding 9.1%, Wang Xiaoqi holding 7.5%, Dalian Jinshi Oil Co., Ltd. holding 29.2%, and Wang Zhengliang holding 16.7%. The legal representative remained Wang Xiaoli, Chairperson of the Board. On August 29, 2004, the shareholders changed to: Wang Xiaoqi holding 45%, Wang Zhengquan holding 55%. The legal representative changed to Wang Xiaoqi, Chairperson of the Board. On July 2, 2007, the shareholders changed to: Dalian Hualiang Enterprise Group Co., Ltd. holding 55%, Sichuan Jinshi Oil Meal Co., Ltd. (legal representative Wang Zhengliang) holding 45%. The legal representative changed to Wang Zhengliang, Chairperson of the Board and General Manager.

Tianyuan Company was originally named Fujian Jinshi Bio-protein Technology Co., Ltd., established on September 29, 2003, as a Sino-foreign equity joint venture between Fujian Jinshi Company and Yifeng Hong Kong Limited, with Fujian Jinshi Company holding 72% and Yifeng Hong Kong Limited holding 28%. The legal representative was Wang Zhengliang. On September 29, 2004, the equity structure of Fujian Jinshi Bio-protein Technology Co., Ltd. changed. The Chinese shareholder changed from Fujian Jinshi Company to Dalian Jinshi Iron and Steel Co., Ltd., Dalian Jinshi Bio-protein Technology Co., Ltd., Dalian Jinzhou Shihe Steel Rolling Co., Ltd., and Dalian Yiliang Trade Co., Ltd. The foreign shareholder changed from Yifeng Hong Kong Limited to Desheng Hong Kong Limited. The company name was also changed to Tianyuan Company. The board of directors consisted of Wang Zhengliang, Zhang Jinghe, and Liu Feng, with the legal representative being Liu Feng. The legal representatives of both Yifeng Hong Kong Limited and Desheng Hong Kong Limited were Liu Feng. On January 15, 2010, Tianyuan Company's name was changed through industrial and commercial registration to Zhongfang Fujian Company. Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd. made a paid-in capital contribution of RMB 24 million on October 15, 2009, accounting for 80% of the equity in Zhongfang Fujian Company. The other shareholders were: Dalian Jinhui Steel Casting Co., Ltd. holding 6%, Wang Xiaoli holding 4.6%, Wang Xiaoqi holding 4.6%, and Wang Zhengliang holding 4.8%.

Wang Xiaoqi, Wang Xiaoli, and Wang Zhengliang are in a parent-child relationship (Wang Xiaoqi and Wang Xiaoli are daughters of Wang Zhengliang). Wang Xiaoqi and Liu Feng are husband and wife.

In the Audit Report submitted by Tianyuan Company, Xiamen Shengyuan Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. audited the balance sheet of Fujian Jinshi Company as of December 31, 2006, the income statement (statement of changes in shareholders' equity) for the year 2006, the cash flow statement, and the notes to the financial statements. In the notes to the financial statements, the land use rights (intangible assets) in the balance sheet of Fujian Jinshi Company for the year 2006 showed an opening balance of RMB 4,687,940.40 and a closing balance of RMB 4,587,663.60. In the cash flow statement of Fujian Jinshi Company, the net cash received from the disposal of fixed assets, intangible assets, and other long-term assets was RMB 18,267,500.17. In the balance sheet of Fujian Jinshi Company, the fixed assets column indicated: original cost of fixed assets: RMB 44,042,705.75; accumulated depreciation: RMB 11,687,872.05; net value of fixed assets at the beginning of the year: RMB 32,354,833.70; at the end of the year: RMB 4,019,622.98; plus construction in progress, total fixed assets at the beginning of the year: RMB 33,254,653.78; at the end of the year: RMB 4,919,443.06.

Cargill Company filed this lawsuit before the court of first instance, requesting: (1) a declaration that the Contract for Sale of State-owned Land Use Rights and Assets signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Zhongfang Fujian Company is void, or alternatively, rescission of Fujian Jinshi Company's act of transferring all its fixed assets to Tianyuan Company for no consideration or at an undervalue; (2) an order that Tianyuan Company return to Fujian Jinshi Company all property acquired under the aforementioned contract, etc. During the proceedings at first instance, Cargill Company clarified that the first request was for a declaration that the Contract for Sale of State-owned Land Use Rights and Assets signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Zhongfang Fujian Company is void.

On March 3, 2010, Cargill Company applied to the court of first instance for property preservation. The court of first instance issued a ruling to seal up the state-owned land use rights originally numbered Zhang Fa Guo Yong (2002) Zi No. 0002 and other assets under the name of Zhongfang Fujian Company. During the process of sealing up the state-owned land use rights, it was confirmed by the Zhangzhou Branch of the Zhangzhou Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources that the parcel of land had been transferred to Huifengyuan Company in March 2008, and the land use rights registration had been changed accordingly. Upon investigation, Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company signed a Contract for Sale on February 21, 2008, stipulating that Huifengyuan Company would purchase the land use rights over the 32,138 square meters of land, as well as the buildings and structures and equipment thereon, for a total price of RMB 26.69 million, consisting of a land price of RMB 6.03 million, a building price of RMB 3.34 million, and an equipment price of RMB 17.32 million. Huifengyuan Company obtained the state-owned land use rights certificate for the said land in March 2008, with the certificate number Zhang Fa Guo Yong (2008) Zi No. 0021. Huifengyuan Company paid Tianyuan Company RMB 5.69 million on April 7, 2008, and did not pay the remaining amount thereafter.

Huifengyuan Company was established on February 19, 2008, with a registered capital of RMB 5 million, of which Song Mingquan contributed RMB 3 million and Yang Shuli contributed RMB 2 million. On September 16, 2009, Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd., Song Mingquan, and Yang Shuli signed a Share Transfer Agreement, stipulating that Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd. would contribute RMB 4 million to purchase 80% of the equity in Huifengyuan Company. On the same day, Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd. (Party A), Huifengyuan Company (Party B), Song Mingquan and Yang Shuli (Party C), and Shenyang Jindou Food Co., Ltd. (Party D) signed a Share Pledge Agreement, stipulating that Song Mingquan and Yang Shuli would pledge their 20% equity in Huifengyuan Company to Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd. as security for the performance of "contractual obligations" by Party B, Party C, and Party D. "Contractual obligations" referred to all responsibilities and obligations arising from the "Red Bean Incident" under the Share Transfer Agreement and the Share Pledge Agreement for Party B and Party C. The "Red Bean Incident" referred to a series of lawsuits and arbitration disputes involving the Jinshi Group arising from the admixture of red beans in imported soybeans by Cargill Company, as well as a series of lawsuits and arbitration disputes involving Huifengyuan Company related thereto. The Share Transfer Agreement also provided that the "contractual obligations" of Party B and Party C would be deemed fully performed when the following circumstances simultaneously occurred: (1) all litigation and arbitration proceedings arising from the "Red Bean Incident" had been fully concluded and enforced, and Party B had not suffered property losses; (2) any possible right of rescission by Cargill Company against the contracts involved with Party B had been extinguished due to expiration of the maximum statutory period (five years). On November 1, 2009, Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd. contributed RMB 4 million and obtained 80% of the equity in Huifengyuan Company on November 18, 2009. The legal representative changed to Wang Zhaohui, the directors were Wang Jin and Wang Zhengliang, and the supervisors were Zhang Jinghe and Liu Yanhua.

The court of first instance added Huifengyuan Company as a third party in this case. Subsequently, Cargill Company brought the following claims against Huifengyuan Company: (1) a declaration that the Contract for Sale of State-owned Land Use Rights and Assets between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company is void; (2) an order that Huifengyuan Company return the property obtained under the contract to the property owner.

The court of first instance investigated Gao Wentian, the Chief Financial Officer of Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Zhang Hongyi, the Manager of the General Management Department. The investigation records showed that when Zhongfang Grain and Oil Import and Export Co., Ltd. acquired the companies under the Jinshi Group, it also packaged and acquired Huifengyuan Company. After its establishment, Huifengyuan Company only purchased one piece of land, paid Tianyuan Company RMB 5.69 million, and thereafter had no actual business operations and no money in its accounts. Its annual financial statements were prepared by Zhongfang Fujian Company on its behalf. Huifengyuan Company had no office premises of its own and merely borrowed an office from Zhongfang Fujian Company.

The court of first instance held that: Cargill Company initiated this lawsuit on the grounds that the Contract for Sale of State-owned Land Use Rights and Assets between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company was the result of malicious collusion, impairing its lawful rights and interests, and sought a declaration of voidness and return of property. Therefore, the cause of action should be classified as a dispute over a sales contract. Since Cargill Company's place of registration is in Switzerland, this case is a foreign-related civil and commercial dispute. Pursuant to Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-related Civil and Commercial Cases and Article 4 of the Provisions of the Fujian High People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-related Civil and Commercial Cases in the Courts of the Province, this case falls within the jurisdiction of this court. Both parties agreed that the laws of the People's Republic of China should apply, so the laws of the People's Republic of China shall be the governing law.

Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China specifies the statutory circumstances under which a contract is void, including "malicious collusion causing harm to the interests of the state, a collective, or a third party." Therefore, the focus of dispute in this case is whether the asset sale contracts between Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company involved malicious collusion that harmed the lawful rights and interests of Cargill Company, thus warranting a declaration of voidness and return of property. This issue should be determined by considering the following aspects:

(1) Whether Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company are related

Article 217 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Affiliated relations refer to the relationships between a company's controlling shareholders, actual controllers, directors, supervisors, senior management personnel and the enterprises they directly or indirectly control, as well as other relationships that may lead to the transfer of company interests." The evidence in the case shows that Wang Xiaoqi, Wang Xiaoli, and Wang Zhengliang are in a father-daughter relationship, and Wang Xiaoqi and Liu Feng are in a husband-wife relationship. From the establishment of Fujian Jinshi Company to the signing and performance of the State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract involved in this case, the legal representatives were either Wang Xiaoli or Wang Zhengliang, and the shareholders were composed of Wang Xiaoqi, Wang Xiaoli, Wang Zhengliang, and their father-daughter team, as well as Dalian Jinshi Oil Processing Co., Ltd., and the actual controller of Dalian Jinshi Oil Processing Co., Ltd. was also the father-daughter team. At the time of its establishment, the legal representative of Tianyuan Company was Wang Zhengliang, and the shareholders were Fujian Jinshi Company and Yifeng Hong Kong Co., Ltd. (legal representative: Liu Feng). After the shareholder change on August 29, 2004, the board of directors consisted of Wang Zhengliang, Zhang Jinghe, and Liu Feng, with Liu Feng as the legal representative. It can be seen that during the signing and performance of the State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract, the controlling shareholders of both Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company were Wang Xiaoqi (Liu Feng), Wang Xiaoli, and Wang Zhengliang (father-daughter). Fujian Jinshi Company and China Textile Fujian Company fell under "the relationship between the actual controller and the enterprises directly or indirectly controlled by them," and should be recognized as affiliated relations.

After its establishment, Huifengyuan Company only purchased the land use right involved in the case, had no office space of its own, and engaged in no actual business operations. The directors of Huifengyuan Company were Wang Zhengliang, and the supervisor was Zhang Jinghe. Wang Zhengliang and Zhang Jinghe were both directors and supervisors of Huifengyuan Company and simultaneously the legal representative or board members of Tianyuan Company. The purpose of establishing Huifengyuan Company was solely to purchase the land and assets involved in the case under Tianyuan Company's name, and it essentially operated as "one set of personnel, two signboards" with Tianyuan Company. The sales contract between the two companies could potentially lead to the transfer of Tianyuan Company's interests, meeting the circumstances of affiliated relations as defined by the aforementioned legal provisions.

(2) Whether Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company were aware of the debts involved in this case

Jinshi Group had a long-term commercial cooperation with Cargill. In 2004, due to financial difficulties, Jinshi Group failed to pay Cargill for goods in a timely manner. During the FOSFA arbitration process, Cargill and Jinshi Group reached a Settlement Agreement, stipulating that Jinshi Group would repay the debt of USD 13.37 million in installments over five years and would mortgage all assets of Fujian Jinshi Company, including land use rights, buildings and fixtures, all equipment, and other property, to Cargill as security for the repayment of the aforementioned debt. Wang Zhengliang signed the Settlement Agreement on behalf of five companies, including Fujian Jinshi Company, Dalian Jinshi Oil Processing Co., Ltd., Shenyang Jinshi Soybean Industry Co., Ltd., Sichuan Jinshi Oil Meal Co., Ltd., and Yifeng Hong Kong Co., Ltd. Liu Feng was both the legal representative of Yifeng Hong Kong Co., Ltd., a debtor under the Settlement Agreement, and the legal representative of Tianyuan Company. Although Yifeng Hong Kong Co., Ltd. transferred its 28% equity in Tianyuan Company to Desheng Hong Kong Co., Ltd. on August 29, 2004, the legal representative of Desheng Hong Kong Co., Ltd. was also Liu Feng. Given the familial relationship among Wang Xiaoqi, Liu Feng, and Wang Zhengliang, and especially the affiliated relationship between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, it should be recognized that Tianyuan Company should have known about the entire development process of Jinshi Group's debt of USD 13.37 million to Cargill and the agreement in the Settlement Agreement to mortgage all assets of Fujian Jinshi Company to Cargill.

According to the Share Pledge Agreement between China Textile Cereal, Oil and Foodstuff Import and Export Co., Ltd., Huifengyuan Company, Song Mingquan, Yang Shuli, and Shenyang Jindou Food Co., Ltd., Huifengyuan Company, Song Mingquan, and Yang Shuli agreed to use equity pledges to guarantee all responsibilities and obligations arising from the "Red Bean Incident," and also mentioned "the possible right of revocation of Cargill with respect to the contract involving Huifengyuan Company." Clearly, Huifengyuan Company was also aware of the facts that the "Red Bean Incident" gave rise to Jinshi Group's debt of USD 13.37 million to Cargill and the agreement in the Settlement Agreement to mortgage all assets of Fujian Jinshi Company to Cargill.

(3) Whether the contract transfer price was reasonable and whether consideration was actually paid

According to the balance sheet of Fujian Jinshi Company as of May 31, 2006, the original cost of fixed assets was RMB 44,042,705.75, minus accumulated depreciation of RMB 11,687,872.05, resulting in a net fixed asset value of RMB 32,354,833.70, and the value of intangible assets (state-owned land use rights) was RMB 4,687,940.40. However, in the State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and China Textile Fujian Company on May 8, 2006, the buildings and equipment were only valued at RMB 21.05 million, which is significantly different. Furthermore, the Appraisal Report from Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. was not issued until November 20, 2006. The price agreed upon by Fujian Jinshi Company and China Textile Fujian Company was clearly not based on the subsequently issued Appraisal Report, thus lacking a reasonable basis.

Although Fujian Jinshi Company provided a bank transfer slip for RMB 25 million dated June 15, 2006, the payment did not specify its purpose and was not the agreed transfer price of RMB 25.69 million under the contract. Moreover, according to the financial statements of Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company for that year, neither the entry nor the expenditure of the RMB 25 million was reflected; instead, it showed that Tianyuan Company still owed Fujian Jinshi Company "other payables" as high as RMB 121,224,155.87. Under these circumstances, it cannot be proven that this payment was used to pay the transfer price under the contract.

Huifengyuan Company obtained the land use right certificate for the land involved in the case and paid corresponding consideration. However, the price for the buildings and equipment as agreed in the Sales Contract was not paid, and there was no evidence of registration, transfer, or actual delivery. Therefore, Huifengyuan Company did not acquire ownership of the buildings and equipment involved in the case.

(4) Whether there was malicious collusion between Fujian Jinshi Company, China Textile Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company to harm the legitimate rights and interests of Cargill

As mentioned above, Jinshi Group still owed a huge debt to Cargill in 2004. As one of the debtors, Fujian Jinshi Company agreed to use its land, factory buildings, equipment, and other assets as mortgage security for the said debt. However, it not only failed to actively cooperate with Cargill in registering the asset mortgage with the relevant authorities, but also ignored the Settlement Agreement between the parties and signed the State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract with Tianyuan Company, transferring the land, factory buildings, equipment, and other assets that should have been mortgaged to Cargill to Tianyuan Company. As a related enterprise of Fujian Jinshi Company, Tianyuan Company was fully aware of the background of the debt. The transfer price agreed upon by both parties was significantly low, and there was insufficient evidence to prove that Tianyuan Company had paid corresponding consideration. Based on the above analysis, Fujian Jinshi Company's intention to evade debts was evident, and the transfer of assets between it and Tianyuan Company should be deemed an act of malicious collusion and debt evasion. The affiliated relationship between Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company demonstrates that the purpose of the Sales Contract between them was solely to transfer the assets involved in the case under Tianyuan Company's name, which also constitutes an act of malicious collusion and debt evasion. The relevant agreement between China Textile Cereal, Oil and Foodstuff Import and Export Co., Ltd. and Huifengyuan Company regarding "the possible right of revocation of Cargill with respect to the contract involving Huifengyuan Company" further proves that Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company had the subjective intent of malicious collusion and debt evasion. The signing and performance of the asset sales contracts between Fujian Jinshi Company, China Textile Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company meant that Fujian Jinshi Company actually became a shell company, which obviously led to the inability to realize Cargill's claims against Fujian Jinshi Company and even Jinshi Group, directly harming the legitimate interests of Cargill. Cargill has the right to file a lawsuit with the court to confirm the invalidity of the contracts and request the return of property.

In summary, the acts of malicious collusion and debt evasion between Fujian Jinshi Company, Tianyuan Company, and Huifengyuan Company infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of creditors and should not be protected by law. The State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, and the Sales Contract between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company should be confirmed as invalid contracts. The property obtained by Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company as a result should be returned to Fujian Jinshi Company. As Tianyuan Company had been changed by industrial and commercial registration to China Textile Fujian Company on January 15, 2010, its claims and debts should be borne by the post-change China Textile Fujian Company. In accordance with Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 52(2) and 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: 1. Confirm that the State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company on May 8, 2006, and the Sales Contract signed between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company on February 21, 2008, are invalid contracts; 2. Huifengyuan Company shall, within thirty days from the effective date of the judgment, return to Fujian Jinshi Company the state-owned land use right obtained under the said contracts, certificate number Zhangfa Guoyong (2008) Zi No. 0021; China Textile Fujian Company shall, within thirty days from the effective date of the judgment, return to Fujian Jinshi Company the buildings and equipment obtained under the said contracts. The court acceptance fee for the first instance of RMB 170,250 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be jointly borne by Fujian Jinshi Company, China Textile Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company.

Fujian Jinshi Company, China Textile Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company all disagreed with the first-instance judgment and appealed to this court, alleging: 1. The first-instance judgment violated legal procedures. (1) After the first-instance court added Huifengyuan Company as a third party on its own initiative, Cargill raised a claim against Huifengyuan Company. Since Cargill had clearly raised a claim against Huifengyuan Company, Huifengyuan Company's procedural status should have been that of a defendant. The first-instance court did not change Huifengyuan Company's status to defendant and directly ordered the third party, Huifengyuan Company, to bear civil liability; (2) One of Cargill's claims against Huifengyuan Company was to request Huifengyuan Company to return property to the "property owner." This claim did not specify to whom the property should be returned, failing to meet the requirements for filing a lawsuit under the Civil Procedure Law; (3) The evidence collected by the first-instance court on its own initiative, including industrial and commercial registration materials and investigation transcripts of witnesses Zhang Hongyi and Gao Wentian, were not cross-examined in court, yet these evidences were used as the main basis for ordering the third party, Huifengyuan Company, to bear the responsibility of returning property.

2. The first-instance judgment's findings of fact were unclear. (1) The first-instance judgment's finding that "Jinshi Group failed to pay the plaintiff for goods due to financial difficulties" leading to a series of commercial disputes between the parties lacked factual basis and improperly determined the background facts of the dispute. In fact, the dispute arose because the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine issued an order prohibiting international grain traders, including Cargill, from exporting soybeans to China, forcing Jinshi Group to cancel its import soybean contracts with Cargill; (2) The first-instance judgment's finding that Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company were "two signboards, one set of personnel, forming an affiliated relationship" was erroneous. The industrial and commercial records show that Huifengyuan Company was established on February 19, 2008. At the time of signing the sales contract on February 21, 2008, its directors were always Song Mingquan, and the supervisor was Yang Shuli. It was not until November 18, 2009, when China Textile Cereal, Oil and Foodstuff Import and Export Co., Ltd. invested in Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company, that the list of directors and supervisors changed. At the time Huifengyuan Company sold the assets, neither Tianyuan Company nor Wang Zhengliang, Zhang Jinghe, etc., had any relationship with Huifengyuan Company; (3) The first-instance judgment's finding that "after its establishment, the third party Huifengyuan Company only purchased the land use right involved in the case, had no office space of its own, and engaged in no actual business operations" was erroneous. Huifengyuan Company is an independent legal entity lawfully established with its own property and premises, having no connection with the companies associated with the two witnesses, Gao Wentian and Zhang Hongyi. The situation described by the two witnesses refers to the situation after China Textile Cereal, Oil and Foodstuff Import and Export Co., Ltd. invested in Huifengyuan Company, not at the time the sales contract was signed; (4) The first-instance judgment's finding that the asset values assessed in the Asset Appraisal Report issued by Dalian Daxin Accounting Firm were unreasonable and obviously low, while using the Appraisal Report issued by Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. as the basis for pricing, lacked reasonable basis; (5) The first-instance judgment's failure to recognize that Tianyuan Company paid RMB 25 million as consideration was unfounded. On June 15, 2006, one month after the contract was signed, Tianyuan Company paid RMB 25 million to Fujian Jinshi Company. Although the bank statement as evidence of payment did not indicate the purpose, both the payer and payee have confirmed that this was the consideration for the sales contract, which is sufficient to prove the purpose and nature of the payment; (6) The first-instance judgment's finding that Huifengyuan Company did not acquire ownership of the buildings and equipment involved in the case was unfounded. Tianyuan Company transferred the land use right to Huifengyuan Company according to the Sales Contract and delivered the buildings and equipment to Huifengyuan Company. In the case of movable equipment that has been delivered to Huifengyuan Company, ownership has been transferred; (7) The first-instance judgment's finding that Fujian Jinshi Company, China Textile Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company had the subjective intent of "malicious collusion and debt evasion," turning Fujian Jinshi Company into a shell company, thereby preventing Cargill from realizing its claims against Fujian Jinshi Company and Jinshi Group, lacked evidentiary support and legal basis. Moreover, there are six companies in the Jinshi Group that are debtors of Cargill. Even if Fujian Jinshi Company were considered a shell company, it cannot be concluded that Cargill's claims cannot be realized. Currently, Cargill's lawsuit against a shareholder of Beijing Kema Meijia Cereals and Oils Co., Ltd., a company within Jinshi Group, is being heard by the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, and Cargill's enforcement cases against companies in Jinshi Group are ongoing in Xiamen Intermediate Court. Fujian Jinshi Company still has external claims.

3. The first-instance judgment erred in the application of law. (1) The first-instance judgment, relying on Article 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, ordered Huifengyuan Company to return property to Fujian Jinshi Company, which was an error in the application of law. The parties to the sales contract were Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company. Even if the contract were deemed invalid, Huifengyuan Company should return property to Tianyuan Company, not to Fujian Jinshi Company, which was not a party to the contract; (2) If the first-instance judgment found that the contracts between Fujian Jinshi Company, China Textile Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company "directly harmed" Cargill's interests and constituted a situation of malicious collusion harming the interests of a third party, then according to Article 59 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the property obtained should be returned to the third party, not to Fujian Jinshi Company; (3) Cargill could require China Textile Fujian Company and Huifengyuan Company to bear responsibility or obligations to it, but it had no right to demand that they bear responsibility to Fujian Jinshi Company on the grounds of contract invalidity. The first-instance judgment's order for return of property between China Textile Fujian Company, Huifengyuan Company, and Fujian Jinshi Company lacked legal basis.

In summary, the first-instance judgment had unclear facts, insufficient evidence, erroneous application of law, and violated legal procedures. Therefore, they requested: that the judgment be reversed, Cargill's claims be dismissed, or the case be remanded for retrial.

Cargill responded: 1. The first-instance judgment did not violate legal procedures. (1) According to Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the people's court may, based on facts and law, order a third party to bear civil liability. Therefore, the first-instance court's decision to order the third party, Huifengyuan Company, to bear civil liability did not violate legal procedures; (2) Cargill's claim against Huifengyuan Company to return property to the "property owner" was clear; the property owner is Fujian Jinshi Company. The claim was specific and met the requirements for filing a lawsuit under the Civil Procedure Law. The purpose of the state-owned land use right and asset sales contracts between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, and between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company, was malicious collusion and debt evasion. According to Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, these contracts are invalid, and the legal consequence is the return of property; (3) The first-instance court's collection of evidence on its own initiative, including industrial and commercial registration materials and investigation transcripts of Zhang Hongyi and Gao Tianwen, was subjected to cross-examination by both parties, and both parties did not dispute the authenticity of the evidence.

2. The facts found by the court of first instance were clear. (1) The FOSFA Arbitration Award No. 3929, recognized by the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court, had already confirmed that the Jinshi Group owed Cargill Company a debt of USD 13.37 million. Therefore, the court of first instance correctly found that the Jinshi Group was in financial difficulty and failed to pay Cargill Company for the goods. (2) Huifengyuan Company was established on February 19, 2008, which was after Cargill Company had initiated a lawsuit against Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company alleging that the sales contract was invalid and seeking the return of property from Tianyuan Company. On the very next day after its establishment, February 21, 2008, Huifengyuan Company entered into a sales contract with Tianyuan Company. This shows that the purpose of establishing Huifengyuan Company was to transfer assets for affiliated enterprises. Moreover, Song Mingquan and Yang Shuli are both from Dalian, held positions in affiliated enterprises, and had close relationships with Fujian Jinshi Company, Tianyuan Company, Wang Zhengliang, Zhang Jinghe, Liu Feng, and others. Since 2004, when Cargill Company and the Jinshi Group began to have disputes, through the malicious transfer of assets by Fujian Jinshi Company and the equity changes in Tianyuan Company, to the establishment of Huifengyuan Company, this fully demonstrates the purpose of Fujian Jinshi Company to maliciously evade debts. (3) The court of first instance, exercising its authority, found that Huifengyuan Company did not pay the price agreed in the Sales Contract for the buildings and equipment, and there was no registration of transfer or actual delivery. It found that after its establishment, Huifengyuan Company only purchased the land use rights involved in the case, had no office premises of its own, and did not engage in actual business operations. This is consistent with the facts. (4) The fixed assets item on Fujian Jinshi Company's balance sheet was over RMB 44 million, while the "Asset Appraisal Report" issued by Dalian Daxin Accounting Firm valued them at RMB 25.69 million, a significant difference. Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company signed the sales contract on May 8, 2006, but Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. did not issue the "Appraisal Report" until November 20, 2006. The above appraisal valuations were low and unreasonable, made for the purpose of evading debts. (5) The RMB 25 million "Bank Payment Slip" that Tianyuan Company paid to Fujian Jinshi Company on June 15, 2006, did not state the purpose, nor was it the contractually agreed transfer price of RMB 25.69 million. Moreover, the financial statements of Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company for that year did not reflect the entry or expenditure of this RMB 25 million. Instead, they showed that Tianyuan Company still owed Fujian Jinshi Company "other payables" as high as RMB 121,224,155.87. Therefore, it cannot be said that this payment was used to pay the transfer price under the contract. Furthermore, Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company were affiliated enterprises with numerous inter-company transactions. (6) There were no facts or evidence showing that Huifengyuan Company paid the price agreed in the Sales Contract for the buildings and equipment, or that there was registration of transfer or actual delivery. Therefore, Huifengyuan Company did not acquire ownership of the buildings and equipment involved in the case. (7) Tianyuan Company, knowing that Fujian Jinshi Company owed a debt to Cargill Company and the agreement regarding the mortgage between them, still entered into the sales contract with Fujian Jinshi Company. The transfer price was low, and Tianyuan Company did not even pay consideration. Tianyuan Company and Fujian Jinshi Company are affiliated and had the subjective intent of malicious collusion to evade debts. Any malicious evasion of debts or transfer of assets by any company within the Jinshi Group harms the interests of Cargill Company as a creditor and may lead to the inability to realize Cargill Company's claims.

3. The application of law by the court of first instance was correct. (1) The purpose of the State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, and between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company, was malicious collusion to evade debts. Pursuant to Article 52 of the Contract Law of the PRC, these contracts should be invalid. Pursuant to Articles 56 and 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Cargill Company requested that the property be returned to the "property owner," who is Fujian Jinshi Company. The court of first instance's judgment that Huifengyuan Company return the property to Fujian Jinshi Company has a legal basis. (2) The judgment of the court of first instance required Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company to return property to Fujian Jinshi Company, not that they return property to each other.

In summary, the facts found by the court of first instance are clear, the evidence is conclusive and sufficient, the application of law is correct, and there is no violation of legal procedure. This case should be adjudicated by dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

The facts found by this Court in the second instance are consistent with those found by the court of first instance. Therefore, this Court affirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: This case is a foreign-related case. All parties have no objection to the application of the laws of the PRC to the adjudication of this case, and this Court confirms that.

This case arises from the creditor Cargill Company's claim that the sales contracts regarding the land use rights, above-ground buildings, equipment, and other assets between the debtor Fujian Jinshi Company and its affiliated enterprise Tianyuan Company, and between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company, constitute the circumstances under Article 52(2) of the Contract Law of the PRC of "malicious collusion harming the interests of the state, the collective, or a third party" and therefore should be found invalid, and requests the return of the original property. The court of first instance held that Tianyuan Company and Fujian Jinshi Company are affiliated enterprises, Tianyuan Company knew about Fujian Jinshi Company's debt to Cargill Company, the agreed transfer price for the land use rights, above-ground buildings, and equipment was obviously low, and there was no sufficient evidence to prove that Tianyuan Company had paid that consideration. The affiliation between Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company can prove that the purpose of reaching the "Sales Contract" between them was to transfer the assets that Tianyuan Company had acquired from Fujian Jinshi Company. The performance of these contracts caused Fujian Jinshi Company to become essentially a shell company, directly leading to the inability to realize Cargill Company's claims. Therefore, the asset transfer between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, and the asset transfer between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company, should both be found to be acts of malicious collusion harming the interests of Cargill Company. Accordingly, the court of first instance found that the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company on May 8, 2006, and the "Sales Contract" signed between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company on February 21, 2008, were invalid; Huifengyuan Company shall return the state-owned land use right obtained under the above contracts to Fujian Jinshi Company; Tianyuan Company shall return the buildings and equipment obtained under the above contracts to Fujian Jinshi Company. The disputed issues in this case are: Do the contracts entered into among Fujian Jinshi Company, Tianyuan Company, and Huifengyuan Company constitute contracts of malicious collusion harming the interests of Cargill Company? What are the legal consequences after the contracts involved in this case are found invalid?

(A) Whether the contracts entered into among Fujian Jinshi Company, Tianyuan Company, and Huifengyuan Company in this case constitute contracts of malicious collusion harming the interests of Cargill Company.

First, in the process of signing and performing the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company, their actual controllers were related by family. Moreover, Wang Xiaoqi and Liu Feng, as the legal representatives of Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company respectively, signed the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract". Wang Xiaoqi and Liu Feng are husband and wife. Therefore, it can be found that during the signing and performance of the contract to transfer Fujian Jinshi Company's state-owned land use right, buildings, and equipment, Tianyuan Company was very clear about Fujian Jinshi Company's situation, including the fact that the Jinshi Group, including Fujian Jinshi Company, had been confirmed by arbitral award to owe Cargill Company a debt of USD 13.37 million due to the "Red Bean Incident".

Second, the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" was signed on May 8, 2006, which stipulated that the price for Tianyuan Company to purchase Fujian Jinshi Company's assets was RMB 25.69 million, of which the land use right was valued at RMB 4.64 million and the buildings and equipment were valued at RMB 21.05 million. Dalian Daxin Accounting Firm Co., Ltd. issued an "Asset Appraisal Report" on May 5, 2006, stating that the appraised value of the machinery and equipment assets provided by Fujian Jinshi Company as of the appraisal base date of April 30, 2006, was RMB 15,685,400. Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued an "Appraisal Report" on November 20, 2006, assessing the state-owned land use right, factory buildings, office buildings, and other structures owned by Fujian Jinshi Company at the request of the company, determining the asset value as of the appraisal base date of May 8, 2006, to be RMB 10,004,607. The appraisal report issued by Dalian Daxin Accounting Firm only appraised the machinery and equipment; the appraisal report issued by Zhangzhou Tianzheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. was issued after the date of signing the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract". Obviously, when Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company signed the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract", they did not price based on the appraisal reports from the accounting firms. Therefore, the appeal argument of Fujian Jinshi Company and Zhongfang Fujian Company that the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" was priced based on the appraisal reports of the two accounting firms cannot stand. The court of first instance, based on the balance sheet of Fujian Jinshi Company as of May 31, 2006, submitted during the first instance proceedings, which showed that the original value of fixed assets was RMB 44,042,705.75 and the net value after depreciation was RMB 32,354,833.70, while the price for buildings and equipment in the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" was only RMB 21.05 million, correctly found that the price agreed in the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" for Tianyuan Company's purchase of Fujian Jinshi Company's assets was an unreasonably low price. Given that the transferee Tianyuan Company knew that the debtor Fujian Jinshi Company owed a huge debt to the creditor Cargill Company, its purchase of the main assets of Fujian Jinshi Company at an unreasonably low price is sufficient to prove that Tianyuan Company and Fujian Jinshi Company had subjective malice when signing the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract", constituting malicious collusion, and the performance of this contract is sufficient to harm the interests of the creditor Cargill Company.

Third, after the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" was signed, although Tianyuan Company, on June 15, 2006, transferred RMB 25 million through the Agricultural Bank of China, Zhangzhou Branch, to the account of Fujian Jinshi Company at the same bank, the transfer did not indicate the purpose of the payment. Moreover, on the same day, Fujian Jinshi Company remitted the RMB 25 million in two installments to the account of its affiliated enterprise, Dalian Jinshi Oil Manufacturing Co., Ltd. According to the financial statements of Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company for that year, this RMB 25 million was not reflected as an entry or expenditure. Instead, it showed that Tianyuan Company still owed Fujian Jinshi Company "other payables" of RMB 121,224,155.87. Therefore, it was reasonable for the court of first instance to find that Tianyuan Company did not actually pay the price to Fujian Jinshi Company under the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract". The appeal argument of the appellants Fujian Jinshi Company and Zhongfang Fujian Company that the contract price had actually been paid lacks factual basis and cannot stand.

Fourth, from the company registration materials, the shareholder composition of Huifengyuan Company at the time of its establishment appeared unrelated to Fujian Jinshi Company. However, during the process of equity changes in Huifengyuan Company, it can be seen that when Huifengyuan Company signed the "Sales Contract" with Tianyuan Company, it knew about the source of the assets transferred by Tianyuan Company and the debt of Fujian Jinshi Company to Cargill Company. The price agreed in the "Sales Contract" was RMB 26.69 million, which was not significantly different from the price at which Tianyuan Company purchased the assets from Fujian Jinshi Company. Except for the RMB 5.69 million already paid by Huifengyuan Company to Tianyuan Company, the remaining amount was not paid. The court of first instance was correct in finding that Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company acted with malicious collusion when signing the "Sales Contract", which was sufficient to harm the interests of the creditor Cargill Company. Whether Huifengyuan Company actually engaged in business activities, and the witness testimony of Gao Wentian and Zhang Hongyi, have no substantial impact on the above reasonable conclusion made by the court of first instance. Therefore, the appeal argument of the appellants Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company that the court of first instance incorrectly described the situation of Huifengyuan Company and that there was no malicious collusion between Huifengyuan Company and Tianyuan Company cannot stand, and this Court does not support it.

In summary, the "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company on May 8, 2006, and the "Sales Contract" signed between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company on February 21, 2008, are contracts constituting malicious collusion harming the interests of Cargill Company. Pursuant to Article 52(2) of the Contract Law of the PRC, both shall be found invalid. The court of first instance correctly found this. The appeal argument of the appellants Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company that there was no malicious collusion and that the interests of Cargill Company were not harmed thereby cannot stand, and this Court does not support it.

(B) Regarding the legal consequences after the contracts involved in this case are found invalid. For the treatment of invalid contracts, the people's court shall first, pursuant to Article 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC, which states: "After a contract is found invalid..., any property acquired under the contract shall be returned; if return is impossible or unnecessary, compensation shall be made at an appraised price. The party at fault shall compensate the other party for any losses incurred thereby; if both parties are at fault, each shall bear its own liability," order the party that acquired the property to return it. The "State-owned Land Use Right and Asset Sales Contract" signed between Fujian Jinshi Company and Tianyuan Company on May 8, 2006, and the "Sales Contract" signed between Tianyuan Company and Huifengyuan Company on February 21, 2008, involved in this case, are both found invalid. The property involved in the two contracts is the same. The state-owned land use right has been transferred from Fujian Jinshi Company through Tianyuan Company to be held in the name of Huifengyuan Company. In the absence of evidence proving that the buildings involved in this case have been transferred from Tianyuan Company to Huifengyuan Company's name and that the equipment involved has been delivered by Tianyuan Company to Huifengyuan Company, it is not inappropriate for the court of first instance to directly order Huifengyuan Company, which acquired the state-owned land use right, and Tianyuan Company, which acquired the buildings and equipment, to return the property they each acquired to Fujian Jinshi Company. The appellants Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company did not provide sufficient evidence to prove that the buildings and equipment involved have all been acquired by Huifengyuan Company. Therefore, their appeal argument that even if property must be returned, it should be returned by Huifengyuan Company, lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Article 59 of the Contract Law of the PRC states: "Where the parties maliciously collude..., harming the interests of a third party, the property acquired as a result shall be returned to the third party." This article should apply to situations where the third party can be identified as the owner of the property. In this case, Cargill Company has a general creditor's claim against Fujian Jinshi Company. The property involved in this case is the property of Fujian Jinshi Company, not the property of Cargill Company. Therefore, the judgment can only order the disputed property to be returned to Fujian Jinshi Company, and cannot directly order its return to Cargill Company. The court of first instance correctly applied Article 58 of the Contract Law of the PRC in handling this case. The appeal argument of the appellants Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company that this case should be governed by Article 59 of the Contract Law of the PRC and that the court of first instance erred in its application of law cannot stand, and this Court does not support it.

(C) Regarding the legal status of Huifengyuan Company in this case. Given that Cargill Company, as the plaintiff in the first instance, made clear claims against Huifengyuan Company, Huifengyuan Company should be listed as a defendant, not a third party. The court of first instance improperly listed Huifengyuan Company as a third party in this case. However, this procedural defect did not affect the court of first instance's correct judgment on the merits of the case.

In summary, the appeal arguments of the appellants Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company are all untenable. The facts found by the court of first instance are clear, and the application of law is correct. This Court, pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, adjudicates as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The first-instance case acceptance fee and preservation fee shall be borne as determined in the first-instance judgment; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 170,250 shall be jointly borne by the appellants Fujian Jinshi Company, Zhongfang Fujian Company, and Huifengyuan Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Chen Jizhong

Judge: Gao Xiaoli

Acting Judge: Shen Hongyu

August 22, 2012

Clerk: Zhang Bona

Senior Judge Chen Jizhong: Born in 1968, Master of Laws. Appointed as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2007.
